blurb: Lawrence G. McDonald is a former high-yield bond trader at Lehman Brothers, where he worked until the firm's bankruptcy in September 2008. He subsequently wrote 'A Colossal Failure of Common Sense' (2009), a widely-read insider account of Lehman's collapse that became a New York Times bestseller. McDonald later founded The Bear Traps Report, a subscription macro-research service aimed at institutional investors, and built a significant following on financial Twitter (now X) under the handle @Convertbond. His commentary spans US macro, credit markets, convertible bonds, and increasingly equity-market sentiment. The handle reflects his professional background in convertible-bond markets — hybrid securities sitting at the intersection of corporate debt and equity. McDonald's voice on X tends toward sober pattern-recognition: he favours charts, data lists, and rhetorical questions over hot takes, making him a reliable signal among finance-Twitter's noisier participants.
credibility_note: McDonald's market commentary draws on genuine institutional fixed-income experience and a credible track record of identifying credit-market stress signals. His public calls are not audited, and like most macro commentators he has a mix of correct and incorrect directional calls; he is better understood as a lens for credit-and-equity risk framing than as a precise market timer. His Lehman memoir has been praised for accuracy by other participants but is necessarily a partial account. His work through The Bear Traps Report is paywalled; the X feed represents a curated sample of his output.
